findings.title: canView() ignores the all-clients MANAGE permission, so global managers fail realm-level view checks
findings.body: `canManage()` (line 73) returns true for an all-clients MANAGE permission, but `canView()` only checks `canViewClientDefault()` and the VIEW scope. V1 (`ClientPermissions.java:287-289`) treats manage as implying view. Take an admin whose only grant is all-clients MANAGE: `requireView()` fails at `RealmAdminResource.java:1197` and `ClientInitialAccessResource.java:123`. `canViewClientScopes()`/`requireViewClientScopes()` is false (`RealmAdminResource.java:241`, `ClientScopesResource.java:93`), even though `canManageClientScopes()` is true. `RolePermissions.java:167` also relies on `canView()`. `canView(ClientScopeModel)` (line 121) already ORs VIEW with MANAGE. Do the same here: `|| hasPermission(MANAGE)`.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission searches by a type the per-client resources never get
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates the per-client resource without calling `setType` (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:103-111`). Only the resource-type resource gets a type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:250`). So `findByType(server, "Clients")` can only match the `Clients` type resource. A per-client grant is never returned, and an all-clients grant returns the literal name `"Clients"` instead of client IDs. V1 avoids this by setting the type to `"Client"` when it creates each resource (`ClientPermissions.java:132`). Any caller that narrows results by this set silently gets the wrong answer. Either set the type on per-client resources, or look them up some other way.

findings.title: In V2, deleting a client leaves its permission resource behind
findings.body: With V2 on, the new guard skips the listener entirely, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws anyway (line 193). Nothing removes the resource named after the deleted client's UUID, or the scope permissions that reference it, from the admin-permissions resource server. Those orphaned permissions stay listed and keep being evaluated. Consider a V2-specific cleanup on `ClientRemovedEvent`.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: Nothing uses the private `getEvaluationContext` (line 262), the `logger` field (line 51), or the imports `Scope` and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` / `ClientModelIdentity` (only the dead method uses the last one). Remove them.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods says "Returns true"
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 95-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) return void and throw ForbiddenException. Their Javadoc says "Returns {@code true} if ...". Reword it to match the other require* docs. The `canView()` Javadoc should also mention MANAGE once that check is added.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The PR adds a Clients resource type and ClientPermissionsV2. I found two likely bugs, both medium confidence. First, V2 canView() ignores all-clients MANAGE, unlike V1, so admins who can manage clients are denied realm-level view and client-scope view checks. Second, getClientsWithPermission searches by a resource type that per-client resources never get. Minor: orphaned V2 client permissions after a client is deleted, dead code, and Javadoc wording. I read the test files and found nothing to flag.

**Batch 2 of 2.** No findings for this part (`UserResourceTypePermissionTest.java`). The change is mechanical: every call now passes the injected `client` to the new static helpers in `AbstractPermissionTest`, which hit the same admin-permissions client's scope-permission endpoints as before. The resource-count assertions in `testDelete` count `SCHEMA.getResourceTypes()` at run time, so they still hold now that the schema has more resource types.
